extracted.intended_audience: writers, critics, and students of humor theory; humorists and comic performers seeking principles for producing or analyzing humor
extracted.subtask_description: Theory-driven guidance on creating and recognizing effective humor (practical and poetic), with criteria for repartee, puns, naive blunders, physical mime, and poetic incongruity. Useful for writers, comic performers, and editors who shape funny material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to take disappointment playfully
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor often arises when 'a disappointment which for some reason we are able to take playfully.' We laugh when an expected event is transformed into a nothing from the standpoint of that expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion distinguishes comic perception from mere schadenfreude: the audience must be able to treat the disappointment lightly (distance, imagined/remote victims, or removed stakes help). Example: families stuck in a vehicle whose horse won't move become comic because the thwarted purpose enlarges into absurdity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical humor as absurdity (reduction to absurdity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical humor is often 'an absurd situation' or a 'reduction to absurdity' of the whole attitude of our wills — planned purpose brought to nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing practical jokes, aim to set up an active expectation and then frustrate it in a way that makes the absence itself comic (e.g., preparations that culminate in non-event). Keep actions concrete and situational so the audience experiences the thwarted purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irish bull (plausible-appearing emptiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'Irish bull' is 'any remark which appears rotund and meaningful enough, until our apprehension actually arrives upon it, when there is simply nothing there.' Its plausibility distinguishes it from pure nonsense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this device when you want a joke that seems logically plausible until inspection reveals vacuity. The charm can be in the finely developed plausibility and graceful landing of an intellectual nothing (Lewis Carroll examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as stumbling-and-finding (discovery within joke)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit often combines a seeming failure with a discovery: 'To stumble and find something is to enjoy a joke.' A witty joker contrives to trip us so we find a hidden 'gold piece' (a clever insight or reversal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a joke to be witty rather than merely absurd, include a positive payoff — a recovered meaning, a clever twist, or an unexpected insight that the audience discovers in the stumble (example: Sumner's rejoinder to the minister).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of repartee
rubrics_metrics.description: Repartee follows a conversational game: one contestant propounds a thesis that gives him glory or his opponent ignominy; the opponent manipulates the thesis so the propounder’s glory disappears and his own appears; the contest continues until one 'cries enough.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful repartee requires quick manipulation of implications, escalating reversals, and rhythm between the players. Aim for moves that neutralize the opponent's boast and recast it as your victory — rapid alternation and restoration attempts are part of the game's pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eluding censorship / saying indirectly
rubrics_metrics.description: One source of wit is the 'eluding of a censorship': saying indirectly what good manners would prohibit directly, so the offense is carried by the opponent's logic rather than by crude insult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use implication and indirect phrasing to convey a brusque sentiment elegantly. The humor often lies in letting the opponent's own premises carry them to a comic outcome (e.g., turning an insult into a logical consequence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of the naive blunder (innocent error)
rubrics_metrics.description: Naive blunders (innocent mistakes) can give both a shock and 'a rich and positive pleasure' — affection, sympathetic delight, or realization of a wish. They present not only the failure but the person (their innocence) and so invite love or pity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using naive errors in comedy, foreground the human, sympathetic element; audience enjoyment increases if the blunder reveals earnestness or vulnerability (schoolboy definitions, children’s misstatements). These are often more 'beautiful' than deliberate wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity: 'really happened' matters
rubrics_metrics.description: A humorous incident that 'really happened' is often funnier than the same incident offered as a contrived 'funny story.' Real-life occurrences, told with a mood of serious belief, have a special virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic editors and writers should favor authentic anecdotes or present contrived material as if it were genuine. The mood of belief and the force of reality increase the comic impact (the 'bell for recess' effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pun evaluation: negative action vs affirmative recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The pun's pure negative action is the nonsensical use of a word; puns merit respect only when they 'offer some good strong joy in the recovery.' 'A pun shall do something more upon the affirmative side than merely make a little sense.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid puns that are mere vacuous wordplay. To make a pun satisfying, arrange for a meaningful secondary sense or an affirmative payoff that rewards the audience for the linguistic shift; otherwise the pun feels graceless and alien.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbal absurdity often alien to immediate humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Words are usually containers of meaning; when they fail (verbal absurdity), the audience must abandon expectations and perform an act of recognition, so puns and wordplay often startle admiration more than produce visceral humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that verbal jokes often require a pause and reflective recognition; they are less immediate than situational or poetic incongruities. Use them sparingly or ensure they carry additional emotional payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic humor as playful disconcertion of naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic humor is 'a playful disconcertion of this art [of calling names].' Poetry uses words that 'feel' and poetic humor arises when naming is playfully inappropriate or incongruous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To craft poetic humor, manipulate naming — choose feeling-words that are inappropriately applied or juxtapose names to evoke incongruous associations (e.g., calling whiskey 'fire-water' or creating affectionate misnamings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two methods of poetic humor: salient detail & incongruous comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic language makes vivid either by (1) choosing a salient detail or flavor on which to focus, or (2) comparing the thing with another by some salient resemblance. In poetic humor these become (a) inappropriate choice and (b) incongruous comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sharp, salient details to name characters or things unexpectedly (inappropriate choice) and create similes/metaphors that pair mismatched emotional atmospheres (incongruous comparison). Examples: O. Henry's 'lobsters perished' phrasing; Aristophanes' 'voice like a pig on fire.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic incongruity can be non-derogatory and multi-colored
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruous poetic images need not degrade the valued subject; they may increase comic effect by combining qualities oddly (e.g., pancakes counted like money) and can provoke lingering, variegated laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't assume incongruity must be scornful. Employ incongruity to create rich, nuanced comic emotion — mix pathos, wonder, grotesque and delight rather than simple derision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical/visual humor: vivid mimetic acting
rubrics_metrics.description: A key principle in physical humor (Charlie Chaplin example) is 'acting as though a present thing were something else' so vividly that the absent thing 'flashes actually before us.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In visual/comic acting, commit to mimetic detail and believable gestures so the audience perceives the absent object vividly. The humor comes from the actor's convincing conviction, not merely from falling or pratfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: playfulness required; excessive solemnity kills humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor 'depends upon playful-ness and implies it'; an intrusion that is 'too intensely solemn or devout cannot be humorously perceived.' Both ends of a humorous simile must be lightly taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a light, playful tone when presenting incongruity. Avoid moralizing or excessive gravity when the comic effect depends on elasticity of feeling; ensure the audience is invited to play rather than judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic humor's capacity to provoke laughter without a point
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic jokes 'differ in their more enduring ability to provoke laughter without a point.' A mere incongruity presenting an actual thing (not just vacancy) can tickle more strongly and often than a mere bull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aiming for poetic humor, accept that not every joke needs a sharp 'point'; well-crafted incongruity or image can sustain laughter. Favor concrete, image-rich incongruities that present 'an actual thing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine affirmative values to enrich naive humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Naive blunders can supply affirmative satisfactions (loving an innocent mind, glorying over it, or realizing a wished-for thing). Any of these 'affirmative values may flow in to enrich our enjoyment of a naive blunder.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately highlight secondary pleasures—sympathy, triumph, wish-fulfillment—when presenting innocent errors to deepen comic reward and broaden appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediacy vs. objectification: practical vs. poetic balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical humor tends to be immediate and situational (negative, abrupt disappointment), while poetic humor is more lingering, objectifiable, and capable of being enjoyed as a quality in things rather than merely a perceived element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select style according to desired effect: for instant, situational laughs set up thwarted intention and crisp reversals; for enduring, reflective humor craft lasting images, metaphors, and incongruities that can be revisited.
